summary: This sermon explores Jonah chapter 1, emphasizing that the story is not about a whale or hiding from God, but about a prophet's willful rebellion against God's command to preach repentance to Israel's enemy, Nineveh. Jonah knew God would forgive the Assyrians if they repented, and he refused to participate in that mercy, preferring they be destroyed instead.
key_points: Jonah was Jeroboam II's prophet who led Israel in syncretistic idol worship
He fled to Tarshish (opposite direction from Nineveh) to frustrate God's plan of mercy
The pagan sailors feared God more than the prophet did
Jesus used the sign of Jonah to point to resurrection and God's offer of salvation to all nations
Israel was destroyed by Assyria because Israel never repented, not because Nineveh did
big_idea: God calls us to surrender our self-interest and national pride to participate in His mission of extending mercy and forgiveness to all people, even our enemies.
title: JONAH: Rebellion & Repentance
